subject: Post-call: Dedicated pool + isolation needs for Stride AI
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@strideai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — Dedicated pool + isolation needs for Stride AI

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please reply if I missed or mischaracterized anything.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Current model serving (on-prem + cloud) is brittle at scale: long tail latency spikes when batch jobs overlap with inference traffic.
- Data isolation and PHI handling are strict requirements for their clinical pilots — procurement will require explicit isolation and audit logs.
- Cost predictability is a priority for Q4 budgeting; they expect to cap weekly spend and need clear throughput guarantees.
- Goal: 50k requests/day initially, 200k/day in 6 months, tail P95 latency < 300ms for top-line routes.

Redwood fit / proposed configuration
- Reserved Dedicated pool (single-tenant GPUs) with tenant isolation for PHI workloads.
- Autoscaling buckets + burst policy for spiky batch windows (we recommend a 2-tier burst for 4x short bursts).
- SLA ask: 99.5% uptime on dedicated pool; P95 latency objective scoped per-route (we propose 300ms baseline for the generation route).
- Operational controls: per-route token caps, prefix caching for stable prompts, and canary rollout hooks.

Open questions we need from Stride
1) Exact throughput distribution (sync vs. async) and typical prompt lengths (avg/95th token).
2) Any mandatory compliance docs beyond SOC 2 (PCI? HIPAA BAAs?) — Caroline from procurement to confirm.
3) Timeline constraints for procurement / PO signing — do they target Live by Nov 1?

Next steps (mutual action plan)
- Rachel: Share a short MAP doc + SOW draft by Mon 07/27 (attached).
- Ben: Prepare a pricing snapshot for reserved pool (3 sizes) + burst add-on (due Tue 07/28).
- Priyom: Internal ops sizing note + isolation reference architecture for their PHI flows (due Mon 07/27).
- Alex / Caroline: Send sample throughput profile and confirm compliance gate list by Wed 07/29.

Attachments included: StrideAI-MAP-0719.docx (mutual action plan), SOW-draft-v1.pdf (commercial draft), isolation-arch-3up.png (ops diagram).

Thanks again — I’ll follow up Monday with the MAP and the SOW stub.

—
Rachel Kim
Senior Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0127
[Attachment: StrideAI-MAP-0719.docx (DOCX, 28KB)]
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@strideai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Caroline Liu <caroline.liu@strideai.com>, procurement@strideai.com
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Dedicated pool + isolation needs for Stride AI

Thanks Rachel — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:
- Throughput profile: today roughly 20k requests/day (mostly short prompts, avg 60 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens). We expect a monthly doubling for the next three months as the pilot expands.
- Compliance: HIPAA applies for clinical pilot (we will need a BAA). We also run annual penetration tests and need access to some audit logs for sample exports.
- Timeline: Procurement is targeting a Nov 15 go-live for the pilot (conservative). PO cycle typically 6–8 weeks after final SOW.

We’ll attach a sample throughput CSV and compliance checklist later today. Quick question: can you confirm whether Redwood supports HSM-backed key management in Private deployments? If not, what are the isolation guarantees in Dedicated?

—
Alex Turner
Head of Infrastructure | Stride AI
alex.turner@strideai.com
[Attachment: stride_throughput_sample.csv (CSV, 4KB)]
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 08:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: initial ops sizing + KMS notes for Stride AI

Folks — follow-up internal note after Alex’s reply. High level items to include in the SOW and ops recap:
- KMS/HSM: Dedicated (hosted) does not currently surface customer-managed HSMs; Private (VPC/on-prem) path supports HSM integrations (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM) and can be included for BAAs. For Dedicated we can offer envelope encryption + customer-managed keys in our control plane, but if they require BYOK with HSM we should push Private deployment.
- Isolation: single-tenant GPU pools with hypervisor-level tenant separation + network microsegmentation. We should propose a dedicated subnet, private routing, and restricted egress for PHI workloads.
- Sizing: Given current 20k/day and 2–3x monthly growth, propose starting with a 4-GPU reserved pool (A100-style equiv), with an ops-managed burst bucket of +8 GPUs for short windows (2–4 minute bursts).
- Expected cost range (ballpark): reserved baseline ~ $XXk / month (we’ll put concrete numbers in Ben’s pricing snapshot), burst increments billed hourly.
- SLAs: Ops agrees to 99.5% uptime for the pool and an SLO for P95 route latency at 300ms; will draft fallback policy to route to a compatible quantized variant if isolation pool reaches capacity.

I’ll attach a quick architecture diagram and the template SOW language I plan to propose. Priyom

—
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
[Attachment: isolation-arch-3up.png (PNG, 95KB)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Dedicated pool + isolation needs for Stride AI

Alex / Caroline — looping in commercial pricing as promised. I’ve attached a high-level pricing snapshot and two optional add-ons: (1) Burst capacity guard (pre-warmed GPUs) and (2) Extended observability retention for audit exports.

Quick bullets:
- Recommended starter: 4-GPU reserved pool + burst (8 GPUs available on demand). Estimated baseline list: $42,000 / month (reserved) + burst usage.
- BAA / Compliance add-on: we can sign a BAA and enable extended audit exports (billing impact noted separately).
- Procurement path: standard Redwood SOW + PO. If procurement needs shorter payment terms or specific audit items, let us know and I’ll route to finance.

Next steps: Rachel will send finalized MAP + SOW; we’ll update numbers in the SOW once we get the throughput CSV.

—
